sources.entry: Scientific Benchmarking of Parallel Computing Systems - Sets which mean fits costs, rates and ratios, when confidence intervals are owed, and the absolute base a speedup needs.

summary.title: Scientific Benchmarking of Parallel Computing Systems
summary.one_liner: Learn which mean to use for costs, rates and ratios, when to report confidence intervals and variation, and why speedup needs an absolute base-case time.
takeaways: Use the arithmetic mean only for costs such as execution time, and the harmonic mean for rates such as flop/s.
Avoid averaging ratios; average the underlying costs or rates instead, and use the geometric mean only if those are unavailable.
When reporting speedup, state whether the base case is a single parallel process or the best serial run, and give its absolute performance.
Report units unambiguously, distinguishing flop (count) from flop/s (rate) and base-2 from base-10 prefixes.
Show variation and all results rather than only the best run, since nondeterministic runtimes can hide important spread.
summary.summary: The paper is a guideline document from ETH Zurich on reporting performance results for parallel computing systems. It starts with a literature survey of 120 papers from three HPC conferences (HPDC, SC, PPoPP, 2011–2014), finding that reports often lack variation measures, averaging methods and software details. It then gives practical rules: speedup should carry its base case and absolute numbers, units should be unambiguous, subsets and cherry-picking should be avoided, and summaries should match the data type. The data-analysis section explains algebraic summaries for deterministic counts and why costs, rates and ratios need different means, illustrated with a worked HPL example. The page text is cut off before the confidence-interval and experimental-design sections.
